Find the horizontal asymptote of \( f(x)=\dfrac{3x^2+1}{x^2-4} \).

Both numerator and denominator have degree 2; ratio of leading coefficients: \( y=\dfrac{3}{1}=3 \).

body.en: A piecewise function uses different rules for different intervals. A recursive function is defined by its previous terms: e.g. \(a_1 = 2\), \(a_n = 3a_{n-1} - 1\). Parametric equations express \(x\) and \(y\) as separate functions of a parameter \(t\).

Eliminate \(t\) from \(x = t+2\), \(y = t^2 - 1\).

From \(x = t+2\): \(t = x-2\). Substitute: \(y = (x-2)^2 - 1 = x^2 - 4x + 3\). Parabola.

label.en: ▲ ACT Math 2 Traps & Pitfalls — Rational, Piecewise & Inverse Functions

body.en:
• Holes vs. Vertical Asymptotes: If a factor cancels from both numerator and denominator, it creates a removable hole \((c, y_0)\), NOT a vertical asymptote. A vertical asymptote occurs ONLY where the reduced denominator equals zero.
  • Piecewise Boundary Conditions: When evaluating piecewise functions at domain boundaries (e.g. \(x = 0\)), check the inequality symbols carefully (\(<\) vs. \(\le\)) to apply the correct rule.
  • Inverse Function Domain & Range Swap: The domain of \(f^{-1}\) is the range of \(f\), and the range of \(f^{-1}\) is the domain of \(f\). A function only has an inverse function if it is strictly one-to-one (passes the horizontal line test).
  • Composite Function Order: \((f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))\) means evaluate \(g(x)\) first, then substitute that output into \(f\). In general, \(f(g(x)) \neq g(f(x))\).

question.en: A function is defined piecewise: \(f(x) = x^2\) for \(x < 0\), and \(f(x) = 2x+1\) for \(x \geq 0\). Find \(f(-3) + f(2)\).
Let \(f(x) = \dfrac{3x + 4}{x - 2}\) for \(x \neq 2\). (a) Determine the equations of all vertical and horizontal asymptotes of \(f(x)\). (b) Derive the inverse function formula \(f^{-1}(x)\).

solution.en:
(a) Asymptotes: Vertical asymptote: denominator zero \(x - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 2\). Horizontal asymptote: degrees of numerator and denominator are both 1, so \(y = \dfrac{3}{1} = 3\).

(b) Inverse function: Set \(y = \dfrac{3x + 4}{x - 2}\). Solve for \(x\): \[ y(x - 2) = 3x + 4 \implies xy - 2y = 3x + 4 \implies xy - 3x = 2y + 4 \implies x(y - 3) = 2y + 4. \] Thus \(x = \dfrac{2y + 4}{y - 3}\). Swapping variables: \(f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{2x + 4}{x - 3}\) for \(x \neq 3\).
